column1: # scripts/hugmesh-view.tsv — the LOCAL BROWSING catalog: which front doors
# `scripts/hugmesh-view.py` can put in this machine's browser, and on which
# loopback port each one lands.
# WHY THIS FILE IS A FILE. Every HugMesh front door routes by HOST HEADER
# (the kind ingress serves `hugmesh.net` + `*.hugmesh.net`; Harbor serves
# `registry.hugmesh.net`), so `http://localhost:8443/` 404s and the names do
# not resolve without an /etc/hosts entry — which needs root. hugmesh-view
# solves that by serving HTTPS on 127.0.0.1 under a loopback-only CA this user's
# own browsers trust, and speaking HTTPS upstream with the right Host header.
# WHICH host, WHICH upstream and WHICH loopback port is policy, not code: a mesh
# with more domains just gets more rows here.
# Format: one door per row, exactly SIX TAB-separated columns:
#   <name>  <lane>  <host>  <upstream>  <local_port>  <path>
#   name        stable id. Also names the port override env var:
#               HUGMESH_VIEW_PORT_<NAME>, uppercased with '-' -> '_'
#               (so `app` -> HUGMESH_VIEW_PORT_APP=9190 moves it).
#   lane        which set of doors this row belongs to; `--lane` / `make view
#               LANE=…` selects exactly one, and `kind` is the default:
#                 kind        the HOST SHELL, and nothing else. One port.
#                 kind-svc    the platform's internal UIs (ArgoCD, Vault,
#                             Casdoor, Harbor). Deliberately NOT in `kind`:
#                             every one of them is meant to be reached THROUGH
#                             the shell, and a standing row of side ports is how
#                             a broken federated route goes unnoticed until
#                             production. Opt in when debugging the platform.
#                 compose     the tests/stack compose lane's front doors.
#                 device      a live emulated device's own front door.
#   host        the Host header the door routes on, and the hostname rewritten
#               back to the loopback origin in redirects, cookies and bodies.
#               '-' for a door that does not route by name (a port-forwarded
#               ClusterIP service answers whatever Host it is given).
#   upstream    where the door actually listens. The SCHEME picks the mechanism:
#                 https://H:P            talk straight to it (self-signed OK)
#                 http://H:P             ditto, plaintext
#                 k8s+https://NS/SVC:P   `kubectl port-forward`, then proxy
#                 k8s+http://NS/SVC:P    (ClusterIP-only services: no ingress)
#                 device+https://LABEL   `ssh -L` into a live emulated device,
#                                        then proxy. LABEL may be `@gateway`,
#                                        which resolves to the running device
#                                        carrying the mesh's front door.
#               `${VAR:-default}` is expanded from the environment, so the
#               compose rows honour the same PUBLIC_*_PORT knobs compose does.
#   local_port  default loopback port the browser opens. Overridable per row
#               (see `name`) — a port collision is a one-line fix, never an edit
#               to this file.
#   path        the path worth opening (printed in the table). '-' means '/'.
# To ADD a domain: append a row. Nothing else. `hugmesh-view.py list` will show
# it, `up` will serve it, and any OTHER door's redirect to that hostname is
# rewritten to its loopback port automatically (that is what keeps an SSO round
# trip inside the tool instead of escaping to a name the browser cannot
# resolve).
# '#' lines and blank lines are ignored. Columns are TABS, not spaces.
# ── kind lane: THE HOST SHELL, and nothing else ──────────────────────────────
# The kind node publishes 443 -> host 8443 (specs/cluster/bootstrap/kind-local/
# kind-local.yaml), and the internal ingress routes by name. This one row is the
# whole default lane on purpose: the shell is the product, and every user-facing
# surface behind it is a federated remote reached THROUGH this port.
app
# ── kind-svc lane: the platform's own UIs, opt-in ────────────────────────────
# `--lane kind-svc` (or `--only harbor-portal`) when you are debugging the
# platform rather than using the product. Harbor has a real Ingress of its own;
# the rest are ClusterIP-only, so they are reachable only through a
# port-forward. argocd-server serves TLS on 443 and 307-redirects http -> https
# on whatever port it is handed, so it needs the proxy in front to terminate;
# the other three are plain http behind it.
registry
argocd
casdoor
vault
harbor-portal
# ── compose lane (tests/stack/compose.local.yaml) ────────────────────────────
# The plain door is already plaintext; it is here so the fe-gateway sees
# `Host: hugmesh.net` and emits the absolute URLs it would emit in the cluster.
# The TLS door is fronted so the browser never meets its per-machine CA.
compose-app
compose-tls
# ── emulated-device lane (tests/qemu keep-alive devices) ─────────────────────
# A keep-alive device publishes ONLY ssh on 127.0.0.1:22300-22399, so its web
# UI is reachable only through an ssh -L tunnel to the guest's own :443.
device-app
